voiceover: Can you trust the Bible — or has it been changed beyond recognition over two thousand years? This section takes the reliability question apart, piece by piece. Thousands of manuscripts let scholars reconstruct what was originally written, and see exactly where copies differ. That establishes faithful transmission — a separate question from whether the content is true. Archaeology, the Dead Sea Scrolls, and small undesigned coincidences keep showing the text meeting the real world it claims to describe. The tab makes the case that the Gospels are early and rooted in eyewitness memory, and that they carry the personal names that actually fit first-century Palestine. The alleged contradictions and the question of how the canon was chosen are raised plainly, then answered. Every one of these arguments gets a fully-cited deep-dive essay. Each claim is sourced, and the strongest objections are stated fairly, then answered. That is our standard — Checked Before Published. And you will not just read. On every essay an AI tutor answers your questions — ask it anything, or highlight a single sentence and ask about that exact line. Mastery mode lets you explain the argument back in your own words and have it graded. Daily practice brings the key points back just as you are about to forget them. There are pocket cards to share, and a Debate Arena to practise against an AI sceptic before the real conversation. Every essay comes in a plain-English version and a full deep dive, with read-aloud audio. None of this by itself proves the Bible true — that is a further question. What it makes the case for is that the text you hold is essentially what was written: a reliable record to weigh, not a corrupted one. Start anywhere, and follow it where it leads.
